info.title: AquaTome fish ID
info.description:
A reader's photo → Claude's guesses → the handbook's pages for them, for the site's tool (/vi/cong-cu/nhan-dien-ca/) and the iOS app (apps/site/worker/fishid/api.ts).

GET says whether the tool is on, and its daily limits.

POST comes one of two ways:
- The site's page: same-origin (`Origin`), with a Turnstile `token`. Counted per address: `perIp` a day.
- The app: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, the token a sign-in with client "app" returns (protocols/accounts.openapi.json), checked as GET /api/v1/session checks it. No Origin and no Turnstile. Counted per account (`perAccount` a day, kept 24 h), not per address: many phones share one carrier address. A bearer that is present but missing, expired or signed out is `401 {error: "session"}`, even with a `token` too: it never falls back to the page's way.

Every identification also counts against the site's day (`busy` past it).

The photo: JPEG, PNG or WebP, at most 1.5 MB. Send it shrunk (the page sends a JPEG of 1024 px at most) and without its metadata (location, camera). It goes to Claude, Anthropic's model, and is not logged; the log keeps counts, timings, the model, tokens and keys by hash only.

Keeping (the reader's opt-in, one per photo, unticked by default: "Cho phép AquaTome giữ ảnh này để cải thiện nhận diện"): with `keep`, a JPEG is kept with its result for 6 months, private (only the site's admins see it), its own metadata cut, then deleted. It is kept under the account that sent it (the app's bearer, or the page's signed-in cookie), or, sent signed out, tied to no one. The answer then says `kept`: false when it wasn't (not a JPEG, or storage unavailable); the identification stands either way. Every answered photo is kept when asked, `other` and refusals (`unclear`) too: they are results to check. Without `keep`, nothing is stored and the answer has no `kept`. The account lists and deletes its kept photos with GET /api/v1/fish-id/photos and DELETE /api/v1/fish-id/photos/{id} (protocols/accounts.openapi.json); they go when the account is deleted.

Our own copies (a user agent with `AquaTomeCheck/1`) are answered as anyone's, but their guesses add no wanted names.

Errors are `{error}`; the app shows each with the site's own words for it (apps/site/src/scripts/fish-id.ts).

The agent (the Worker's `FISH_ID_AGENT`): Claude checks its guesses against the handbook before it answers, by searching it and opening pages to compare their photos with the reader's. The answer has the same shape, plus `steps`, what it looked at. With the agent off there are no `steps`. An identification can take up to 45 s with the agent: give the request at least 60 s.

Progress (`Accept: text/event-stream`): the answer comes as server-sent events, `200 text/event-stream`, but only once the photo is admitted. Every refusal before that (400, 401, 403, 413, 415, 429, 503) is the JSON error with its status, as without the header. On the stream: `event: step` (zero or more, a `Step` each), then `event: result` (the `Identification`, the same body as the JSON answer, `steps` included) or `event: error` (an `Error`: failed | unavailable | resting), and the stream ends. A `: ping` comment line comes every 10 s while Claude works, never after the result. With the agent off the stream has no steps, then the result. Send the header always. Recorded streams for a fake server, each checked against this contract by the Worker's tests: protocols/fishid-stream-agent.sse (the agent: a search, two pages, a ping, the result), protocols/fishid-stream-off.sse (the agent off), protocols/fishid-stream-failed.sse (an error after the stream began), and protocols/fishid-rate.json (the reader's day used up: the JSON refusal, with its status, that comes instead of a stream).

Retries (`Idempotency-Key`, a UUID the app makes per photo it sends): the run goes on if the connection drops, and its result is kept 15 minutes under the reader and that key. A retry with the same key gets that result (as JSON, or as one `result` event) with no new identification and no new count. A retry while the first is still running is a new identification.

The reader's day: an identification counts when it is admitted, so parallel requests can't pass the limit, and one that ends with no result (failed, unavailable, resting) gives its count back.

get.summary: Whether the tool is on, and its limits

post.summary: Identify the fish or plant in a photo

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: One per photo sent: a retry with the same key within 15 minutes gets the first run's result, not a new identification.

200.description: Claude's guesses, each with the handbook's pages for it

schema.description: Server-sent events, asked for with `Accept: text/event-stream`: `step` events, then one `result` or `error`, then the end; `: ping` comment lines between them. Each event's data is one line of JSON, of the schema `x-events` gives for its name.

429.description: Error: rate (the reader's day is used up: `limit` says how many it has) | busy (the site's day, or its spend, is)

bearer.description: The app: the token from a sign-in with client "app" (protocols/accounts.openapi.json).

Status.description: {on: false} when the tool is off; otherwise its Turnstile site key (the page's way), whether every key is resting, and the daily limits.

resting.description: Every key is set aside for now: an identification would answer 503 resting.

perIp.description: Identifications a day for an address (the page's way).

perAccount.description: Identifications a day for an account (the app's way).

file.description: The photo, shrunk and without its metadata.

lang.description: The reader's language: the reasons' language and the pages' addresses. vi when missing.

from.description: Where the reader started: the tool's page, or a tank's "identify by photo" button. For the owner's log only.

token.description: Turnstile's token: the page's way only.

keep.description: The reader ticked the opt-in for this photo: keep it with its result for 6 months. Leave it out otherwise.

image.description: The photo as base64 (a data: URL's prefix is ignored).

keep.description: true: the reader ticked the opt-in for this photo. Leave it out otherwise.

verdict.description: other: no fish or plant in the photo (no results); unclear: one is there but can't be told.

refused.description: Claude declined to answer: verdict unclear, no results.

kept.description: Only when `keep` was sent: whether the photo was kept.

steps.description: What the agent looked at, in order. Missing when it didn't use the handbook (the agent off, or it answered from the photo alone).

Step.description: One thing the agent did: search, it searched the handbook (`query`: the name or genus it searched for); look, it opened a page (`page`, in the reader's language) to compare its photos with the reader's.

variety.description: A bred form ("Halfmoon"), when Claude sees one.

reason.description: What in the photo points to it, in the reader's language.

page.description: The handbook's page for it: the breed its variety names, else the species or plant.

species.description: The species beside a breed's page.

sameGenus.description: The genus's other species and plant pages, for "not this one?". Never a match.

url.description: The page's address in the reader's language, when it has one there.

limit.description: With rate: the reader's limit a day.

StreamError.description: The stream's `error` event: the identification began and ended with no result. failed: our request or Claude's answer couldn't be used (as a JSON 502); unavailable, resting: Claude can't be reached for now (as a JSON 503). The reader's count is given back.
